status_policy: a candidate is never promoted to a frozen parameter; UNKNOWN carries the concrete missing measurement

frames.cad_frame: CAD model frame, millimetres, as recorded by the STEP/USD measurement tools

identity.note: STEP 250 BREP vertices vs USD 6354 tessellation points differ by construction; the tessellation is the authority for shape, the BREP for analytic radii

bbox_mm.comment: the 48.65 vs 48.79 mm thin-axis gap and the 180.78/157.78 vs 205.99 mm in-plane gap are a measurement-convention difference, reproduced in P1_WHEEL_IDENTITY_205_VS_181.md

centre_mm.frame: CAD model frame (mm), origin = CAD global origin; NOT a chassis datum
centre_mm.why_partial: three constructions agree to ~0.002 mm in the CAD frame, but no recorded chassis datum / mount transform exists, so the centre in the chassis or robot frame stays UNKNOWN

radial_extent_mm.comment: r_max is an outer radius of the widest measured feature, not a proven rolling radius; the radial extent is dominated by the hub bore (r_min)

thin_edge_finding.statement: the r_max feature occupies an axial band of only 0.585 mm, so it is a circular EDGE (rim lip / flange), not a rolling tread of the wheel's full 49.249 mm width

envelope_aliasing.interpretation: the low envelope bins are an ALIASING artefact: the outer circle is tessellated with about 64 vertices (5.625 deg spacing) while the envelope bin is 5 deg, so exactly 8 of 72 bins contain no rim vertex; the measured low bins sit at 45 deg intervals, which matches the beat period (72 / 8 = 9 bins). The outer envelope is therefore a full 360 deg circle within mesh resolution, and the low bins must NOT be reported as a notch in the wheel

not_proven: that the r=103 mm cylinder is the ground-contact (rolling) surface rather than a flange or rim lip
the tyre/tread material, compliance and contact-patch width
the loaded radius under the robot weight

steering_axis_candidate.comment: a vertical (y) circle family of radius <= 40 mm at each corner is consistent with a swerve/steering module, so the CAD pose is one steering configuration, not a fixed wheel orientation

from_cloud_geometry.note: source cloud is mirrored across the named plane, then compared with the counterpart cloud; residual is an exact nearest-neighbour Hausdorff distance in mm

mirror_symmetry.interpretation: the mirror residual 2.0872 mm is NOT read as real asymmetry: it is below the cloud's own nearest-different-vertex distance p95 = 2.9877 mm (the mesh even contains coincident vertices, minimum spacing 0 mm), so the four solids are mirror copies within tessellation resolution. A rotational phase difference of one vertex step cannot be excluded and is not claimed.

wheel_radius.why_unknown: the largest cylinder/circle family at r=103 mm is measured consistently, but nothing in the recorded evidence proves it is the surface the wheel rolls on; it may be a flange or rim lip
wheel_radius.missing_measurement: ground-contact classification of the r=103 mm surface (axial/radial contact band + tread material) and the loaded radius under the robot mass
forbidden: must not be reported as a verified wheel diameter 206 mm
must not be frozen as a physical parameter

spin_axis.scope: direction only, at the single CAD pose recorded; the axle LINE position and the axis under steering rotation are not proven
spin_axis.why_partial_if_any: at least one independent spin-axis estimate missed the 0.5 deg tolerance
spin_axis.missing_measurement: steering DOF / joint axis data and any measured wheel-pose under steering

wheel_centre.why_partial: the centre is measured in the CAD model frame, but no chassis/robot datum transform is recorded, so the centre in the chassis frame remains UNKNOWN
wheel_centre.missing_measurement: authored chassis datum (root frame origin + up axis declaration) and a chassis-frame transform for every wheel

track_width.definition: distance between the two left/right wheel-centre x coordinates in the CAD frame
track_width.why_partial: derived from the wheel centres and therefore inherits the missing chassis datum; also only valid at the recorded steering pose if the modules are swerve drives
track_width.missing_measurement: chassis datum and the steering pose at which the track is defined

wheelbase.definition: distance between the two front/rear wheel-centre z coordinates in the CAD frame
wheelbase.missing_measurement: chassis datum and the steering pose at which the wheelbase is defined

value.evidence: all four wheel centres share one y = -244.0 mm plane (spread 0.000000 mm), so y is the only axis consistent with four coplanar wheels

up_axis.why_partial: the geometric vertical is inferred from wheel coplanarity, not from an authored datum, and it CONFLICTS with the USD stage's declared upAxis
up_axis.missing_measurement: an authored root frame with a declared up axis and gravity direction

wheel_mass_inertia_friction.missing_measurement: vendor mass/inertia properties, tyre compound and friction coefficient; the CAD solids carry no density assignment in the recorded evidence

candidate_rejected.why_rejected: 0.334 m comes from a 90 mm half-height TEST_PROXY box resting on the ground, not from the real wheel geometry

loaded_rolling_height.delta_statement: the P2/P4 collision box half-height 0.090 m differs from the 103 mm circular feature by -13.0 mm, so any chassis height derived from the proxy box is 13 mm too low
loaded_rolling_height.missing_measurement: the real ground-contact radius (loaded radius including tyre compliance)

may_consume_today_parameterised_only.value: unit vector +-x in the CAD frame (direction only)
may_consume_today_parameterised_only.condition: consume as an axis DIRECTION; never as a joint axis line position
must be passed as an explicit parameter tagged candidate=None-verified, with a sensitivity sweep; never written as the physical wheel radius
chassis-frame track stays UNKNOWN until a datum is authored
identity mapping only; a mapping is not a joint and not a motor channel

may_consume_today_parameterised_only.value: use the recorded residuals as a regression bound when re-authoring the four wheels

forbidden_as_frozen_truth: wheel diameter 206 mm / wheel radius 0.103 m as a physical parameter
lift / spawn height 0.334 m as the real rolling height
the P2/P4 collision box half-height 0.090 m as the real wheel half-height (13 mm short)
wheel mass, inertia tensor, friction coefficient and tyre compliance
track width / wheelbase as chassis-frame values
any axle joint axis or motor channel derived from the axis clusters
the USD stage declared upAxis as the gravity direction
the steering DOF existence or reduction ratio
gates_for_p4: P4 must read this JSON and fail closed if a consumed quantity has verdict UNKNOWN and is requested as a frozen value
any wheel radius used for odometry must be an explicit parameter with a candidate tag and a sweep
P4 must not claim real wheel drive from a diagnostic motion source (P3-04)

unknowns.missing: contact classification of the r=103 mm surface + loaded radius
vendor data or a justified proxy
joint definitions and a steering-pose measurement

discrepancies.statement: P2/P4 collision box half-height 0.090 m vs 0.103 m circular feature radius -> 13 mm gap
USD stage declares upAxis Z while the four coplanar wheel centres put the geometric vertical on the CAD y axis
BREP-vertex bbox [48.6527, 180.782, 157.7827] mm vs tessellated cloud bbox [48.791061, 205.991409, 205.991409] mm
